'''Mike Burgess''' was a Decipher-era [[Squadron Members|Squadron Member]], listed as Red 107 from Durham, U.K..<ref name="sm-fan" /> The published fan table marks the slot Retired after Decipher's SWCCG run. [[Trandosite]] interviewed him on 2 May 2000.<ref name="trando-iv2" />

Decipher recruited volunteer Squadron Members in the 1990s to promote SWCCG locally (tournaments, demos, player support). "FL" is printed on some slots in the surviving tables; the tables do not spell out the abbreviation.

== Interviews ==

=== Trandosite, 2 May 2000 ===
Rod Latham interviewed Burgess for [[Trandosite]].<ref name="trando-iv2">[http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/iv2.htm Mike Burgess interview], [[Trandosite]] (2 May 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041026204829/http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/iv2.htm Internet Archive]</ref>

* '''Start in the game:''' A Star Wars fan since childhood, he came back to the films with the re-releases. He bought a Premiere starter deck and played his younger brother before finding decipher.com and the UK player register.<ref name="trando-iv2" />
* '''Early help:''' Mat Allen introduced him to The Kessel Run, and Andrew Sims helped him with the rules. His first tournament was run by John Shields.<ref name="trando-iv2" />
* '''Directing:''' No events ran in the North East of England, so he became a tournament director. His first event, at McNulty's Internet Café in Newcastle, set the local record of 14 players. At its peak Newcastle ran up to three sanctioned tournaments a month.<ref name="trando-iv2" />
* '''Formats:''' He ran Bespin and Beyond events, booster "bingo" games, a carried-over "snowball" jackpot and a Constructed-to-Sealed day.<ref name="trando-iv2" />
* '''Squadron work:''' He directed at Gen Con 99, the 1999 Regionals and the 2000 National Championships.<ref name="trando-iv2" />
* '''Views:''' He disliked how the enhanced cards (EPP, ECC) devalued the standard versions, though he rated EJP highly. He preferred Mains and Toys decks.<ref name="trando-iv2" />
* '''As a player:''' His one major event was the 1998 Gen Con Open Regional, where he finished second from last.<ref name="trando-iv2" />
